- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., > +1.0 for 3+ days), model tends to overestimate continuation — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 periods.
- Model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/– > 0.5) — add 2–5% to forecast for next 2–4 periods.
- If forecast mean is > 70.0 and true outcome is consistently below 68.0, model is overconfident — apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3 periods.
- Sentiment volatility (high std dev) correlates with model lag — adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag in sentiment direction (e.g., if sentiment turns negative, forecast drops 1–2 days later).
